clue.text: Top running bird

parts.note: a cap is a top, as on a bottle or pen
a machine that is running is on

explanation.surface: Someone names the leading bird in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top running' reads as one phrase, a front-runner, but it splits into two pieces before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A castrated cockerel fattened for the table is a kind of domestic fowl.

clue.text: Was he forced to sign on? Study the handwriting

definitions.text: Was he forced to sign on?

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or learn by heart
script is handwriting

explanation.surface: A handwriting expert examines a signature to see if it was made under duress.
explanation.definitionFit: A draftee is compelled by law to enlist in the armed forces.

clue.text: Biased umpire deducting point for Jewish victory

indicators.note: something biased is bent out of true, so the letters left are skewed into a new order
deducting takes the point's letter out of the word umpire before rearranging

parts.note: E (east) is a compass point

explanation.surface: A partial referee docks a point from the side, handing a Jewish team the win.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deducting' removes E (a compass point) from UMPIRE, leaving UMPIR, which 'Biased' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: The festival commemorates the deliverance of the Jews from Haman's plot, told in the Book of Esther.

clue.text: Sort of light tea in mess has just arrived

definitions.note: a verb phrase for a noun: the answer is one who has just arrived

parts.note: neon lighting is one kind of light

indicators.note: tea in a mess is jumbled, so its three letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone describes a cup of tea brewed in the army mess that has only just turned up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in mess' rearranges TEA to ATE. The definition is loose: the answer names a newborn, one who has just arrived.
explanation.definitionFit: A newborn baby, within its first weeks of life, is one freshly come into the world.

clue.text: We hear Annie's former husband is dead!

indicators.note: we hear tells us the phrase is spoken, and its sound gives the letters entered

parts.note: Annie's ex-mate, said as ex-Annie-mate

explanation.surface: Gossip reports breathlessly that Annie's ex has died.
explanation.walkthrough: Annie's former husband is her ex-mate; said as 'ex-Annie-mate' it runs into the rare word for lifeless.
explanation.definitionFit: A rare Latin-derived word for lifeless or inanimate.

clue.text: Call out legal-after start of emergency

indicators.note: after puts the word for legal behind the first letter
the start of a word is its first letter, here of emergency

parts.note: licit means lawful or legal

explanation.surface: A lawful call-out in the opening moments of an emergency.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw out or evoke a response, as a question draws an answer.

clue.text: He's a match for anything!

parts.note: reads as praise for someone able to take on any challenge, but describes a fire-raiser who will put a match to anything

explanation.surface: Praise for someone who can take on any challenge.
explanation.definitionFit: A fire-raiser sets light to property, literally applying a match.

clue.text: Anger in sweetheart

parts.note: an old flame is a former sweetheart

explanation.surface: Fury hidden inside a lover.
explanation.definitionFit: To inflame someone is to provoke or enrage them.

clue.text: Funny stories, so a decent variety show

indicators.note: a variety show is a mix of acts, so the letters of the phrase are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: Amusing tales make a decent variety show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variety' rearranges SO A DECENT; 'show' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Short amusing accounts of real incidents, told as tales.

clue.text: Radio authoress rejects society

indicators.note: rejects means the society letter is thrown out of the woman's name

parts.note: Esther Summerson narrates much of Dickens's Bleak House, a woman writing her own story

explanation.surface: A woman writer turns her back on high society for broadcasting.
explanation.walkthrough: The authoress is ESTHER; 'rejects' drops S (society) from her name.
explanation.definitionFit: Broadcasting is said to go out over the airwaves, the medium once imagined to fill space.

clue.text: Acrostic' puzzle begins with name for drugs

indicators.note: begins with puts the name letter at the front of the rest
to puzzle is to confuse, so the word acrostic is jumbled

explanation.surface: A word puzzle starts with a name and leads to drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Acrostic puzzle' reads as a noun phrase, a word game, but 'puzzle' is the anagram signal and 'begins with' puts N (name) at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Narcotics are opiates and similar substances that dull the senses.

clue.text: Rifle" shooting's internal body

indicators.note: internal means the letters lie inside the words rifle shooting's

explanation.surface: A rifle wound to the internal organs.
explanation.definitionFit: Flesh is the soft substance of the body, as in 'the spirit is willing but the flesh is weak'.

clue.text: Mate steps from deck to cabin

parts.note: a mate is a friend or companion
a ladder is a set of steps

explanation.surface: A ship's mate climbs down from the deck to the cabin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mate' looks like the ship's officer, but it means a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: On a ship, this is the stairway leading from the deck down to the cabins.

clue.text: Popular loaf, said to be natural

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: said tells us the word for a loaf is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a loaf is bread

explanation.surface: A best-selling loaf claims to be all natural.
explanation.definitionFit: Inbred qualities are innate, part of one's nature from birth.

clue.text: Actors with strong accents on the air

parts.note: a broad accent is a strong regional one
the cast is the actors in a production

explanation.surface: A troupe of performers with thick regional accents goes on the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: The charade is in answer order: BROAD first, then CAST, though the clue names the actors first.
explanation.definitionFit: A transmitted programme is sent out over radio or television.

clue.text: Anti-inflammatory 'substance, most effective in an emergency

parts.note: an gives A

indicators.note: in puts the word for most effective inside the distress call

parts.note: SOS is the international distress signal in an emergency
best means most effective

explanation.surface: A medical note on the best anti-inflammatory drug to use in a crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Anti-inflammatory' looks medical but means fireproof: the mineral resists flames. SOS is the distress signal.
explanation.definitionFit: This fibrous mineral was used for fireproofing because it will not burn.

clue.text: A pointer, presumably, to a drying pitch

definitions.meaning: a pointer is a breed of dog, and one stuck to something would be a ...
in cricket, a rain-soaked pitch drying in the sun becomes treacherous for batsmen

explanation.surface: A hunting dog points the way to a cricket pitch drying after rain.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket slang: a sticky dog is a wet pitch drying under sun, on which the ball behaves unpredictably.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket jargon for a difficult, drying wicket; jokily, a gluey hound such as a pointer.

clue.text: Decline to remove wrinkles?

definitions.meaning: to decline is to fall off or lessen
read as ..., to take out creases, as an iron does

explanation.definitionFit: To lessen or fall away; jokily, to iron out folds by de-creasing.

clue.text: Origin of the old poet's'cuirasses

indicators.note: the origin of a word is its first letter, here of the

parts.note: Horace was a Roman poet of the first century BC

explanation.surface: Tracing where an ancient poet's armour came from.
explanation.walkthrough: Horace, the Roman poet, supplies the old poet's name with its 's.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural of the Greek word for breastplate, also the chest region the armour protects.

clue.text: Break down after changing lane, say.

indicators.note: changing alters the order of the letters of lane and say together

explanation.surface: A driver breaks down after switching lanes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Break down' looks like a car failing, but it means examine in detail.
explanation.definitionFit: To analyse is to separate something into its parts to examine them.

clue.text: A cultivated dwarf

parts.note: reads as a refined little person, but means a tree grown small on purpose

explanation.surface: A sophisticated person of short stature.
explanation.definitionFit: A Japanese art of growing miniature trees in pots, kept small by pruning.

clue.text: Leave the room when dismissed with tempers rising

parts.note: a batsman dismissed in cricket is out

indicators.note: rising, in a down clue, means the word for tempers is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a pet is a fit of temper

explanation.surface: Someone storms out after being sacked, tempers flaring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns PETS (fits of temper) up the column to STEP.
explanation.definitionFit: To step out is to go outside, leaving a room for a moment.

clue.text: Having column, like a book

definitions.meaning: having a spinal column, a backbone
a book has a spine, its bound back edge

explanation.definitionFit: Possessing a backbone, as vertebrates do, or a back edge, as bound volumes do.

clue.text: Asian ascent for which climber gets no support

definitions.text: Asian ascent for which climber gets no support

parts.words: Asian ascent for which climber gets no support
parts.note: reads like a mountaineering feat in the Himalayas, but describes a fakir's illusion where a boy climbs an unsupported cord

explanation.surface: A mountaineer tackles an Asian peak without help.
explanation.definitionFit: A legendary illusion in which a cord rises unaided into the air and a boy climbs it.

clue.text: Dean fails to finish the scriptures — he has a block

indicators.note: fails to finish drops the last letter of the dean's name

parts.note: W. R. Inge, the 'gloomy dean' of St Paul's Cathedral
OT is the Old Testament

explanation.surface: A churchman leaves his Bible study unfinished because of a mental block.
explanation.walkthrough: Dean Inge was a famous early twentieth-century Dean of St Paul's in London; 'fails to finish' drops his final E.
explanation.definitionFit: A cast bar of gold or other metal is a solid block.

clue.text: Anthem losing its short opening passage

indicators.note: losing takes the letters of its out of the word for the anthem

parts.note: an introit is a psalm or anthem sung at the start of a service
its gives IT

explanation.surface: A hymn missing its brief opening bars.
explanation.walkthrough: An INTROIT is the anthem sung as a church service begins; 'losing its' drops IT.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief preliminary section, as at the start of a piece of music.

clue.text: It comes by boat to some consumers

definitions.text: It comes by boat to some consumers

parts.words: It comes by boat to some consumers
parts.note: reads like imported goods shipped to customers, but means sauce served from a jug-like dish at dinner

explanation.surface: Goods are shipped to customers.
explanation.definitionFit: The meat sauce is poured from a gravy boat at the table to diners.

clue.text: Provided notes to andante arrangement

indicators.note: a musical arrangement reorders material, so the letters of to andante are rearranged

explanation.surface: A musician adds notes to an arrangement of a slow piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notes' and 'andante' suggest music, but the definition means added commentary.
explanation.definitionFit: A text with added explanatory comments or glosses has been glossed.

clue.text: Document one of The Exploits of Brigadier Gerard?

definitions.meaning: a legal paper proving ownership of property

definitions.text: one of The Exploits of Brigadier Gerard?
definitions.meaning: Conan Doyle's book title names exploits, which are deeds, so each is a deed in a title

explanation.surface: A paper about Conan Doyle's dashing Napoleonic hussar.
explanation.walkthrough: The Exploits of Brigadier Gerard is a Conan Doyle story collection; an exploit is a deed, named in the title.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal paper proving ownership of land; jokily, a deed named in a book's title.

clue.text: There's a smell about the river — it's at the end of the fork

definitions.text: it's at the end of the fork

indicators.note: about means the smell goes around the river letter

parts.note: pong is British slang for a bad smell
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A stink rises around the river where it forks.
explanation.walkthrough: PONG is everyday British slang for a stink.
explanation.definitionFit: A tine is one of the pointed spikes at the end of a fork.
